newsitem.title: CROATIA: Cro. Varteks to privatise to keep Levi's licence.
newsitem.headline: Cro. Varteks to privatise to keep Levi's licence.

text.p: Textile firm Varteks Denim said it would fully privatise by May, after U.S. clothier Levi Strauss & Co warned it might soon withdraw its licence because of the firm's unresolved ownership structure, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
"We intend to privatise (the company) in two months at the latest," Andjelko Herjavec, general director of Varteks, told Zagreb-based Vjesnik daily.
According to 1991 estimates, over one half -- some 300 million kuna (81 million German marks) -- of the concern's basic capital, is still state-owned.
The rest is owned by small shareholders.
Varteks' top managers were told last month Levi Strauss would not extend the 14-year-long cooperation beyond June 30 unless the ownership problem was settled by then.
Herjavec said the company would favour the employees' buyout scheme, under which the management and employees would acquire a majority stake in the company.
Levi's also conditioned the cooperation on better filtration of waste waters produced by the local plant.
Vartex Denim, now employing 550 workers, has operated profitably since 1983. Its prosperity helped maintain other, less lucrative Vartex plants.
The loss of Levi's licence is seen as an indirect threat to some 4,000 jobs in the otherwise relatively prosperous Varazdin region north of the capital Zagreb, Herjavec said.
